A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same survey. Their text, figures, and complete Appendix A tables support reliable comparison after matching relocated material and changed citation suffixes.

before.justification: Figure 3 reports the authors' descriptive analysis of their curated literature: 76 research and 49 non-research entries, supported by Appendix A assignments. These are original data-analysis results; model-performance findings are attributed to cited studies.

after.justification: V2 retains the original literature categorization and counts in Figure 3 and Appendix A. The additional performance findings in Section 6.3 are attributed to other studies.

M1.justification: The reasoning taxonomy, attribute tags, and assignment rules remain unchanged. Section 6.3 adds critical discussion without introducing or revising an algorithm, model, or inference procedure.

E1.justification: The benchmark inventory in Section 6.1 and Table 5 is retained. Additional literature discussion introduces no datasets or task scenarios actually used in new training or evaluation by the survey.

E2.justification: No evaluated comparator set changes. Section 6.3 discusses classical and specialized time-series baselines through citations, without adding a model-versus-baseline experiment.

E3.justification: Existing protocol descriptions remain unchanged. Section 6.3 recommends horizon-wise reporting, leave-one-dataset-out evaluation, and leakage checks, but does not report implementing new evaluation settings.

E4.justification: Neither version presents its own ablation or robustness experiments. Section 6.3 synthesizes cited replication and ablation findings as discussion rather than adding a conducted supplementary analysis.

E5.justification: No run counts, uncertainty estimates, confidence intervals, or significance tests are added or revised. New mentions of seed sensitivity and fixed-seed recommendations do not change statistical reporting practices.

E6.justification: Section 6.3 adds qualitative findings attributed to cited studies, including cross-dataset rank reversals, prompt and shot-order sensitivity, and performance drops under shift or cold start. Figure 3 counts and Appendix A assignments remain unchanged; no new original benchmark scores appear.

T1.justification: The taxonomy definitions are retained, with no added or revised formal assumptions, theorems, proofs, or derivations. The new inductive-bias discussion is qualitative.

C1.justification: The abstract, three introductory contributions, and conclusion retain the same taxonomy, literature-synthesis, and research-agenda claims. The introduction updates its roadmap to mention Section 6.3.

C2.justification: V1 already discusses skeptical position papers and evaluation weaknesses in Sections 6.2.2 and 7. V2 adds focused explanations involving missing temporal inductive biases and limited transfer from text pretraining, with more specific failure conditions and evaluation safeguards in Section 6.3.

D1.justification: The repository link, taxonomy documentation, and appendix assignment information are retained. Section 6.3 supplies general recommendations rather than additional implementation details or disclosures about completed experiments.

R1.justification: Section 6.3 expands the existing skeptical perspective with critical literature such as Cao and Wang (2024), Tang and Ding (2024), and Paleka et al. (2025). Citation-suffix changes and the added preprint entry matching the retained Zhou and Yu publication are not distinct new works.

P1.justification: V2 adds Section 6.3 with two subsections and revises the introduction and Section 6 overview. The remaining narrative, section sequence, and appendix organization are largely preserved.

P2.justification: Figure 2 gains controversy branches and a branch depicting the already-existing Section 7 outlook. Figure 12 gains counter-evidence branches and moves from page 24 to page 25. Other figure designs and appendix table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: Section 6.3 makes the survey's critical appraisal more informative by connecting negative findings to inductive-bias mismatch, transfer limitations, and concrete evaluation safeguards. This improves balance and practical guidance while building on cautions already present in Sections 6.2.2 and 7. The core synthesis and appendix evidence remain stable.
